summary: The idea is plausible and the profile can attribute it: full-layer FA3 at B=16/32 is 94-98% of the shape, about 3x its floor, and the measured 1.3-1.7 TB/s is blamed on the page-size-1 row gather. Pairing heads into one contiguous 128-byte row attacks that directly, and the FA3 kernel's own time in top_kernels separates the mechanism from the extra pad, un-pad and metadata launches, so no companion is needed.
justification: Plausible on H200. The cache is [pages, 1, Hkv=2, 64] FP8, so the two KV heads of a token sit in one aligned 128-byte line. Today two different (request, kv-head) tiles each fetch a 64-byte half of that line at different times, so each pays the per-row page_table indirection and cp.async issue cost. If L2 fills at more than 64 bytes on a miss, both tiles may also pull the whole line, which would double DRAM traffic. That would explain why the 'effective' rate counted on necessary bytes sits at about 1/3 of the floor bandwidth. The profile supports the target: full decode_16 has FA3 at 186.2 of 194.4 us (floor 63.2), decode_32 is 377.9 us against a floor of 126.4, and verify_16/32 are 94-96% FA3. The head mapping is right for both geometries. Under tp8, Hq=16, Hkv=2, G=8, S=1, so FA3 puts all 16 q heads on super-head 0, heads 0-7 in the low half (kv0) and heads 8-15 in the high half (kv1). Under dp, Hq=128, Hkv=16, S=8, giving 16 q heads per super-head with the same grouping. The zero half adds exactly 0 to each logit, and the discarded output half is the other head's P@V. The expected directions agree with TASK.md weights. Each B=16/32 load is about 75-84% full-layer time (16 x 194-383 us against 46 x 21-29 us), so a 20-35% FA3 gain moves those loads about 15-28%. The B=1 loads pay roughly 10-12 us x 16 on loads of about 1.2-1.3 ms, so they get about 12-15% slower; the brief's ~10% is slightly optimistic. The geomean improves only if the FA3 gain at B=16/32 is above about 8-10%. Weakest link: nobody has measured that the 64-byte gather granularity, rather than per-row index and latency limits that pairing leaves unchanged per byte, is what caps FA3. Doubling headdim also doubles the bytes per K/V stage in shared memory. For the hdim-128 FP8 paged non-TMA instantiation, that can cut pipeline stages or change kBlockN, which could offset the larger per-row fetch. Second weakest: this needs an hdim-128 e4m3 FA3 build in the image's sgl_kernel, with pack_gqa working at 16 q heads per kv head. Otherwise it fails cleanly, which is acceptable.
confounders: fused-preattention-triton: no confounding on the target shapes. It is about 1-2 us (about 1%) of full B=16/32 and is untouched; the full-layer FA3 kernel time is read directly. It does interact on B=1: because it writes q as [tokens, Hq, 64], the pad needs zeros plus 2 copies, which is where the expected decode_1/verify_1 loss comes from. If it were absent the same pad launches would follow the parity q cast, so the loss attaches to this change's layering and not to the landed kernel. The follow-up (paired-heads-launch-cleanup) should have this kernel write q_pad directly.

judge scheduler_metadata (not a landed hypothesis but an inherited input): the rebuild uses max_seqlen_k = page_table.shape[1]*page_size, while the judge's used cache_seqlens.max(), so the split cap may differ on decode_16/32. This is intrinsic, because the paired geometry cannot use the old metadata and cache_seqlens.max() would be a host sync. It is also small: LESSONS records that num_splits is only a cap under dynamic varlen split. Any schedule effect would show in the FlashAttnFwdCombine row.
interference: No companion. A gain means the full-layer FA3 kernel row drops on decode/verify_16/32 with sliding flat, which can only come from the paired geometry. A loss splits three ways and the profile separates them: the paired FA3 kernel itself getting slower (the hdim-128 smem/stage trade-off), more combine time (the split schedule, its own row), or pad/un-pad/metadata launch overhead (their own small rows plus the shape-minus-kernel-sum residual, which matters on B=1). An ab-revert of fused-preattention-triton tells us nothing, because it is not on the measured path. A 'pass None instead of rebuilding metadata' control is functionally the same thing: with None, FA3 runs prepare_varlen_num_blocks internally using the same page-table-derived max_seqlen_k, so the launch count and schedule are the same. Recommend the builder simply pass None on decode as on verify, which makes the code simpler and leaves nothing to A/B. A num_splits control would duplicate the queued fa3-num-splits-full-decode. Readout instruction for the harvester: judge on the FA3 kernel's own us on the four full B=16/32 shapes and on per-shape ratios, not on the headline, since B=1 losses can mask a real mechanism gain in the geomean.
rules_flags: None blocking. q_pad is a fixed-shape allocation with torch.zeros, which is graph-safe and does not depend on values. Queries stay E4M3 with identical values. The cache is read in place through a view (no derived caching). Every key is still attended. No host syncs, provided max_seqlen_k is taken from page_table.shape and never from cache_seqlens.max(), or metadata is simply None.
Minor: FA3's 128-wide output is bf16 [tokens, Hq, 128] and half of it is discarded. That is wasted work, not a rules issue, and the kept half is exactly the per-head result.
open_questions: Does the image's sgl_kernel FA3 include the e4m3 hdim-128 forward with paged KV (page_size 1, non-TMA) and pack_gqa at qhead_per_khead=16? If not, every full test fails at dispatch. Harvest as failed, not regression.
For hdim-128 FP8 paged non-TMA, what kBlockN and stage count does FA3 pick against hdim 64? If the stages halve, bytes in flight per SM may not grow as the brief claims.

Is the ~1.7 TB/s really caused by double L2/DRAM fills of each 128-byte line (two heads read separately)? An ncu dram__bytes_read on full decode_32 before and after would confirm or refute the mechanism directly.
B=1 loads: is the loss about 12-15% as estimated, or does the paired FA3 at B=1 (one super-head, so all parallelism comes from splits) also slow down? Read the full decode_1 FA3 row on its own.
